answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB is a retention crisis, not an acquisition problem. memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing—even when effective short-term—materially reduces 30-day retention and does not support sustainable growth; deploying it now would amplify churn among price-sensitive cohorts already at risk. memory_44 shows enterprise sales-assisted flows work but apply to a different segment and require sales capacity. Instead, activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action without retention damage; combined with the confirmed onboarding simplification (memory_86, exp_86: +3% retention), this addresses the actual problem: accounts that are at-risk are those who haven't yet derived enough value to justify renewal at any price. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well in established customers but do not address active churn. A standard_experiment scale on activation_messaging targets at-risk SMB accounts with value-reinforcement nudges, preserving pricing integrity and avoiding the known retention cliff of discounting. This buys time for leadership to develop a sustainable competitive response while the retention cohort proves its viability.
